arguments.summary: Completed-session technical evidence favors NVDA over MU for the 63-session mandate, while both remain conditional continuation setups rather than forecasts. NVDA combines stronger absolute and benchmark-relative 63-session performance with a shallower observed drawdown and a close above the prior 21-session high. MU retains positive 21/63-session momentum but has slipped over five sessions, remains below its prior 21-session closing high, and carries substantially higher path volatility and drawdown. Market was closed; IEX observations are stale single-venue snapshots, so completed SIP closes are the analytical anchors.

claims.text: NVDA's 2026-10-02 split-adjusted SIP close was $233.95. Completed-session price returns were +3.9454% over 5 sessions, +4.2511% over 21, and +19.6369% over 63. The close was 4.54% above SMA20 ($223.786), 7.18% above SMA50, and 16.56% above SMA200. Over the last five sessions SMA20 rose 0.9161%; the close was 1.3385% above the prior 21-session closing high; last-session volume was 1.3382x the prior-20-session median and recent-five-session average volume was 1.1189x that median. The observed 63-session maximum close-path drawdown was -10.5835%. Annualized realized volatility was 14.8821%, 24.8521%, and 38.2473% over 5/21/63 sessions, respectively; these are historical path measures, not forecasts.

Matched 2026-10-02 split-adjusted SIP price-return comparisons: PAIR NVDA/SPY 5=+4.1671 21=+3.6656 63=+17.1931. PAIR NVDA/XLK 5=+2.1418 21=-4.5778 63=+10.7902. Thus NVDA led SPY at every measured window, while versus XLK it led over 5 and 63 sessions but lagged over 21; the recent absolute rebound therefore coexists with medium-window sector lag rather than uniform leadership.

NVDA has the cleaner continuation setup: its price level is above rising averages, has moved through the prior 21-session closing high, and has 63-session leadership versus both SPY and XLK. The competing explanation is a short-term extended move—RSI14 was 82.97—and the 21-session XLK deficit shows that a high price level does not itself establish sector leadership. Sustained closes above the prior-high area with positive recomputed 21- and 63-session relative returns would strengthen continuation; loss of the frozen SMA20 level and negative 63-session excess versus both benchmarks would materially weaken it.

For NVDA's coarse current regime (close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50, positive 21-session return), overlapping historical samples numbered 265. Positive forward-return frequencies were 58.1132%, 58.4906%, and 71.6981% over 5/21/63 sessions versus unconditional base rates of 58.8697%, 61.6954%, and 73.4694% from 637 observations. The regime did not improve positive-return frequency in this finite sample; 63-session conditional outcomes ranged from a -8.4506% p10 to +40.1616% p90. These dependent, selected observations are neither calibrated probabilities nor causal evidence.

Because the market was closed, NVDA's completed SIP close of $233.95 on 2026-10-02 is the price anchor. The latest IEX trade was $234 at 19:59:59.998859 UTC that day, but no IEX quote was available; a single-venue trade is not a consolidated executable quote.

MU's 2026-10-02 split-adjusted SIP close was $1,074.89. Completed-session price returns were -0.6828% over 5 sessions, +12.4268% over 21, and +9.1536% over 63. The close was 4.87% above SMA20 ($1,025.0015), 12.43% above SMA50, and 57.70% above SMA200. Over five sessions SMA20 rose 3.1041%, but the close remained 2.0503% below the prior 21-session closing high. Last-session volume was 1.1404x the prior-20-session median and recent-five-session average volume was 1.2522x. The observed 63-session maximum close-path drawdown was -25.4770%. Annualized realized volatility was 36.5718%, 49.5463%, and 74.5624% over 5/21/63 sessions.

Matched 2026-10-02 split-adjusted SIP price-return comparisons: PAIR MU/SPY 5=-0.4611 21=+11.8413 63=+6.7098. PAIR MU/XLK 5=-2.4865 21=+3.5978 63=+0.3068. MU lagged both comparators over five sessions, reversed to leadership over 21 sessions, and retained 63-session leadership, although its 63-session edge over XLK was only +0.3068 percentage points.

MU's continuation case rests on a sharply rising SMA20, positive 21/63-session absolute returns, and positive 21/63-session excess returns versus both benchmarks. Its opposing path is more consequential than NVDA's: five-session lag, failure to regain the prior 21-session closing high, 74.56% annualized 63-session realized volatility, and a -25.48% 63-session close-path drawdown show that positive endpoint returns masked substantial path risk. A regained prior-high area plus restored positive five-session excess would confirm renewed leadership; a close below the frozen SMA20 with negative recomputed 21/63-session excess would indicate momentum deterioration.

For MU's coarse current regime (close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50, positive 21-session return), overlapping historical samples numbered 306. Positive forward-return frequencies were 59.1503%, 67.6471%, and 79.0850% over 5/21/63 sessions versus unconditional base rates of 57.9278%, 63.4223%, and 71.1146% from 637 observations. Although conditional frequencies were higher in this sample, the 63-session conditional p10/p90 range was -15.9730% to +81.1562%. Dependence, one finite lookback, regime selection, and very wide outcomes prevent interpreting these figures as calibrated probabilities or guarantees.

Because the market was closed, MU's completed SIP close of $1,074.89 on 2026-10-02 is the price anchor. The latest IEX trade was $1,074.71 at 19:59:58.451494 UTC; the IEX bid/ask observed just after 20:00 UTC was $1,030.27/$1,141.62. These stale single-venue observations do not establish a current consolidated executable quote.

On completed-session evidence specifically for the 63-session technical mandate, NVDA is the stronger of the two: absolute return was +19.6369% versus MU's +9.1536%; excess versus SPY was +17.1931 points versus +6.7098; excess versus XLK was +10.7902 versus +0.3068; and maximum close-path drawdown was -10.5835% versus -25.4770%. This is a market-behavior preference only, not a valuation or fundamental ranking, and it would reverse if recomputed matched-window leadership and drawdown behavior reverse.

gaps.description: The empirical forward-return panels use overlapping observations from one finite 2023-12-18 to 2026-07-06 lookback and a coarse three-sign regime. Non-overlapping, out-of-sample, and alternative-regime tests are needed before assigning stronger empirical conviction; this limits probability interpretation but does not block the dated descriptive setup.

One last-session and one recent-five-session volume ratio cannot establish sustained breakout participation. Several subsequent completed closes with recomputed volume, prior-high distance, and matched benchmark excess returns are needed to confirm persistence.

assumptions: All comparisons use matched 2026-10-02 completed sessions, SIP feed, split-adjusted prices, and price returns; dividends are not included.
Moving-average thresholds are frozen observations from 2026-10-02, not future dynamic averages and not trading instructions.
Annualized realized volatility uses sample standard deviation of completed daily close-to-close returns times the square root of 252; it is not a probability or expected return.
Technical preference is limited to the 63-session mandate and excludes earnings, valuation, and policy judgments.
arguments.counter_thesis: NVDA's high RSI and 21-session XLK underperformance could precede consolidation despite strong 63-session leadership. MU could instead reaccelerate because its 21-session benchmark leadership and rising SMA20 remain intact, but its five-session lag, near-flat 63-session edge over XLK, and much deeper path drawdown make that case less confirmed. A broad cross-asset causal confirmation was not established in this role, so both setups remain stock-specific and conditional rather than evidence of a general risk-on regime.

review_conditions.description: NVDA completed split-adjusted SIP close below the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA20 of $223.786 before expiry would weaken the near-term trend interpretation and prompt reassessment of continuation, without by itself proving loss of 63-session leadership.

For NVDA, recompute matched SIP split-adjusted excess returns after subsequent completed sessions. Positive 21- and 63-session excess versus both SPY and XLK would confirm broader leadership; negative 63-session excess versus both would invalidate the present 63-session technical preference.
MU completed split-adjusted SIP close below the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA20 of $1,025.0015 before expiry would weaken the rising-trend setup and elevate the observed high-volatility drawdown risk.

For MU, recompute matched SIP split-adjusted excess returns after subsequent completed sessions. Positive five-session excess versus both SPY and XLK while 21/63-session excess remains positive would confirm renewed leadership; negative 21- or 63-session excess versus both would weaken the continuation case materially.

question_effects.reason: The routed macro question was awaiting Director materiality decision. Accordingly, this memo does not treat the fixed external benchmark set as broad risk-on confirmation and makes no causal cross-asset claim.

agent_report.work_summary: Analyzed the supplied completed-session price panels, exact benchmark comparisons, technical-path measurements, IEX snapshots, and historical regime forward-return panels for NVDA and MU. Cross-checked every 5/21/63-session leadership statement against signed excess returns and separated stale single-venue snapshot observations from completed SIP closes.
main_conclusions: NVDA has the stronger 63-session technical profile: larger absolute and relative gains, a prior-high breakout, and a shallower observed drawdown.
MU's 21/63-session momentum remains positive, but five-session lag, a close below its prior 21-session high, and markedly higher volatility/drawdown make continuation less robust.

Historical regime frequencies are descriptive only: NVDA's current coarse regime did not improve positive-return frequency versus base rates, while MU's did, but both panels use overlapping finite samples and wide outcome ranges.
Neither IEX snapshot is a current executable consolidated quote; completed 2026-10-02 SIP closes anchor the analysis.
agent_report.short_summary: For a 63-session technical mandate, NVDA is the cleaner conditional continuation candidate and MU is the higher-path-risk setup. Confirmation requires sustained matched-window leadership; loss of frozen SMA20 levels would weaken each trend case.
limitations: No causal attribution from returns or volume was attempted.
No valuation, earnings, policy, or fundamental conclusion is included.
Historical forward-return frequencies are not calibrated probabilities and were not independently out-of-sample tested.
The requested cross-asset confirmation question remained unresolved, so leadership is treated as stock-specific.
